title: SDK parity: standardize retry policy (retryable classifier, backoff+jitter, retry budget, context-aware)
author: Mateusz Zielinski
release_notes: Go SDK now retries retryable failures (429/5xx/transport) using the cross-SDK backoff+jitter + retry budget policy while honoring context cancellation and Retry-After. Defaults are conservative; behavior can be customized per-client/per-request.
description:
Context: This PR implements the cross-SDK retry standard for the Go SDK (ADR-0137) to reduce inconsistent behavior vs. Python/TypeScript and to address support issues around 429 handling and timeout/cancel semantics (SUP-9334, SUP-9342). The policy is context-aware, uses exponential backoff with full jitter, and is governed by a retry budget to prevent retry storms.

What’s included: (1) A single retry implementation used across the SDK request path (non-streaming). (2) Retry classifier aligned to the spec: retry on HTTP 429, 500/502/503/504; retry on transport-level failures that indicate a dropped/failed connection (e.g., net.Error temporary/timeouts, connection reset). (3) Respect server guidance where available: parse Retry-After (seconds + RFC1123 date) and use it as a floor for next delay, capped by MaxDelay. (4) Retry budget: a per-request cap on total time spent retrying (default 20s) and max attempts (default 4 attempts total including the initial request). Budget exhaustion returns a typed error wrapping the last failure with retry metadata. (5) Context awareness: if ctx is cancelled or its deadline is exceeded at any point, retries stop immediately and the ctx error is returned (no further sleeps). (6) Observability hooks: optional callback invoked on each retry decision with attempt number, classified reason, computed delay, and response status (if present). No secrets are logged.

Non-goals / intentionally excluded: streaming reconnect/retry semantics (handled in PR-200 / ADR-0138), server-side retries, and automatic retries for non-idempotent endpoints unless the caller explicitly opts in.

API surface changes: a small additive config struct (RetryConfig) on Client options plus a per-request override. Defaults are enabled but conservative and align with the standard.

Testing: adds table-driven unit tests for classifier + delay calculation + Retry-After parsing + budget/cancel behavior. Tests use httptest servers to simulate 429 bursts and 503 flaps and validate request counts and timing constraints.

Docs: inline GoDoc comments updated to document defaults and how to customize/disable retries.

Rollout: this lands behind the new default client options used by the SDK constructors; no breaking change expected. Customers who previously relied on zero retries can set RetryConfig.Enabled=false.

Links: Linear ENG-2488 (Go SDK parity workstream), ENG-2482 (retry policy standard).
commits: sdk/go: add retry config + wiring into request pipeline
sdk/go: implement retry classifier (http + transport) aligned to ADR-0137
sdk/go: add backoff with full jitter + Retry-After parsing
sdk/go: implement retry budget + typed RetryExhaustedError
sdk/go: table-driven tests for retry decisions + context cancellation behavior
docs: update GoDoc for client retry defaults and overrides
changed_areas: errors: typed error for retry exhaustion with metadata
tests: httptest-based retry scenarios (429, 503, transport error)
review_conversation:
Ibrahim Khan: Can we confirm the default max attempts and budget match the cross-SDK doc? Also please ensure we don’t retry on context cancellation vs timeout from transport.

Mateusz Zielinski (author): Defaults set to 4 total attempts and 20s budget per spec draft. For ctx cancel/deadline: we check ctx.Err() before each attempt and before sleeping; if set we return ctx.Err() without wrapping as retryable.

Rafael Mendes (SRE): Two concerns: (1) avoid synchronized retries (jitter) and (2) don’t ignore Retry-After on 429. Also ensure we cap the delay so a single request doesn’t sleep for minutes.

Mateusz Zielinski: Added full jitter (rand in [0, base]) and made Retry-After a floor with MaxDelay cap (default 5s) and Budget cap (20s). Added tests asserting delay <= MaxDelay and that Retry-After is honored.

Tomáš Novák: Transport classifier—be careful with net.Error.Timeout(): that can also be a server slow read. Do we want to treat it retryable by default?

Mateusz Zielinski: Aligned with spec: treat timeouts as retryable only when they occur during connection establishment / request send. For response body read timeouts we don’t retry here (that will be handled by the timeout standard PR). In this PR the transport retryable set is limited to dial/handshake/write failures; added tests with a custom RoundTripper to simulate.

Brian Murphy: Please ensure idempotency guidance is clear. If user is doing POST to completions, retries could duplicate server work.

Mateusz Zielinski: Added GoDoc note: retries are safe for GET/HEAD by default and for POST only when endpoint is documented idempotent or caller opts in via RetryConfig.RetryNonIdempotent=true. Also included request-id propagation unchanged.

Final outcome: approvals from Ibrahim + Rafael + Tomáš after changes; Brian approved after doc clarification.
